label: D2 rare a2->S1 transition after a rewarded trial, late in the episode
explanation: Fires only at D2 (100% of mass), almost only when the agent chose a2 and landed in S1, i.e. a rare a2->S1 transition (in_action=2 and in_state=1 hold 98% of mass; S2 arrivals and a1 choices barely fire). It is also gated by episode position: there is no activity before trial ~65, and the rate rises steeply through trials 70-99. It fires much more when the previous trial was rewarded (in_rew=1 at that trial D1); a2->S1 after an unrewarded trial is the main false positive. These are low-value steps (value < 7.1). Magnitude is highest on the core trial and in late trials. Every variable is observed at D2 (the current state and action inputs, prev reward, trial position), so no future variable is used. Dev: P 0.94, R 0.73, F1 0.82, mass recall 0.89. Without the prev_reward term: P 0.73, R 0.88, mass 0.97. The missed activations are weak a2->S1 steps that follow unrewarded trials or come just before trial 75.

issues: The scores reproduce. Dev: P 0.942, R 0.730, F1 0.822, mass recall 0.887. Test: P 0.946, R 0.712, F1 0.812, mass recall 0.871.

The factual claims hold. Activation mass is 100% at D2, 0% at D1 and GO. in_state==1 holds 100.0% of mass. in_action==2 holds 97.9%, so the 2.1% left is common a1->S1 steps, which are scattered (in_action==1 & in_state==1 & late scores F1 0.06). There are no activations before trial 60 and only 30 in trials 60-69. The rate rises 0.018 -> 0.034 -> 0.050 over trials 70-99. Every activation has value < 7.13. prev_reward==1 holds 91% of mass.

There is one systematic but minor gap, and the explanation already partly mentions it. Rare a2->S1 steps late in the episode after an UNREWARDED trial fire when the agent's value estimate is low. a2->S1 & ep_trial>=75 & prev_reward==0 scores P 0.34 with 8.4% of mass, but adding value<5.22 to that branch brings it to roughly P 0.87. A better description of what gates the feature is 'previous trial rewarded OR value low', not just 'previous trial rewarded'.
Combining the two branches, (in_state==1)&(in_action==2)&(ep_trial>=75)&((prev_reward==1)|(value<5.5)), raises test F1 from 0.812 to 0.863 and test mass recall from 0.871 to 0.969.
The variables are all observed at D2 (value is the agent's own critic output), so no future variable is involved. The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
